_about: V4 scoring weights (instructor-only, never shipped). Turns V2/V3 verdicts and V1 facts into POINTS GAINED and POINTS DEDUCTED, kept as two separate numbers, per phase, each with a reason. Category budgets are the README's (commit a139f4a) and are not ours to change; inside a category each item gets a TIER, and code scales the tiers to the budget. An overlapping failure (an item and a deduction about the same thing) is counted ONCE (user decision Nov 23): such items are tier zero or the deduction is not applied, as noted per line. cannot_tell or flagged verdicts are never scored automatically: they are listed as pending human with the points at stake. Every grade sheet prints this file's sha.
tier_rule: core = what the README's full-credit sentence leads with, or what the rest of the category depends on; standard = the other things that sentence names; minor = work-order detail the sentence does not name; zero = its failure is already a listed deduction (counted once there).
partial_rule: partial = half of the item's points (decision Nov 23, option A; option B, a judge-reported share of sub-requirements, may replace it per item after measurement)

DATA-01.why: full credit leads with 'DBLP plus at least three real linked datasets'

DATA-07.why: samples: Phase 3 work order, not in the full-credit sentence

DATA-08.why: manifest validation: Phase 3 work order, not in the full-credit sentence

DATASETS-FEWER-THAN-THREE.why: about datasets actually USED (reader code); DATA-01 is about datasets LISTED: different failures, no overlap

HADOOP-01.why: no real MapReduce jobs = the deduction HADOOP-REPLACED (up to 3): counted once, there

HADOOP-02.why: full credit leads with 'correct distributed parsing'; every later job reads its output

HADOOP-06.why: full credit: 'coauthor-pair preparation'; the Spark graph is built from these pairs. Wrong or dropped pairs for large teams are the deduction HADOOP-PAIRS-WRONG; this item scores everything else

HADOOP-09.why: partitioner, idempotent paths, compression, determinism: Phase 4 work-order detail

HADOOP-11.why: job contracts documented: Phase 4 work-order detail

HADOOP-12.why: full credit: 'EMR run'. The instructor confirms the cloud run (a repository alone cannot prove it ran on EMR)

HADOOP-REPLACED.why: carries the 'no real MapReduce' failure (HADOOP-01 is zero)

HADOOP-PAIRS-WRONG.why: wrong/dropped large-team pairs; HADOOP-06 does not score this part

SPARK-01.why: full credit leads with 'correct temporal weighted graph'; every metric is computed from it

SPARK-09.why: full credit: 'temporal analysis'; README: 'All metrics must be time-aware'

SPARK-11.why: collecting the graph to one process = the deduction SPARK-ABSENT-OR-COLLECT (up to 3): counted once, there

SPARK-METRICS-MISSING.why: counted once: SPARK-02..08 each lose their own points for a missing metric (together about 1.9 of the deduction's 2)

FACTORY-01.why: full credit leads with 'correct orchestrator and subagent model'

FACTORY-02.why: role files: the subagent model's content

FACTORY-03.why: authority separation (required roles). The reviewer/test-agent separation is judged in the deduction FACTORY-NO-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, not here (each problem is counted in one place)

FACTORY-04.why: full credit: 'one-writer ownership'. Uncontrolled overlap is judged in the deduction FACTORY-OVERLAP-UNCONTROLLED, not here

FACTORY-05.why: full credit: 'hooks, permissions'; the safety floor every phase relies on

FACTORY-09.why: agent catalog: README section 'Agent submission and reproducibility', not in the full-credit sentence

FACTORY-10.why: replay instructions missing/insufficient = the deduction FACTORY-REPLAY-INSUFFICIENT (up to 2): counted once, there

FACTORY-NO-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW.why: judged only here (FACTORY-03 does not score it)

FACTORY-AGENTS-NOT-SUBMITTED.why: full credit: 'submission of every agent'; no item covers it

FACTORY-OVERLAP-UNCONTROLLED.why: judged only here (FACTORY-04 does not score it)

v1_deductions._about: Deductions decided from V1's deterministic facts (no AI). V1 checks give NO gain points: they are structure and process facts that feed these deductions or serve as evidence for a human.

SECRETS.phase: of the commit that added it
SECRETS.rule: a key-shaped value in project files or history -> proposed -4, which the instructor confirms (the value must be a real secret); a value only in tests or phase evidence -> the instructor looks
SECRETS.why: README: 'Secrets committed or displayed: up to 4 points lost'. Obvious placeholders (documentation examples, FAKE/TEST values) are ignored

TESTS.rule: max x (25 - counted) / 25 when fewer than 25 meaningful tests, else 0
TESTS.why: README: 'Fewer than 25 meaningful ... tests: up to 2 points lost'; scaled by how far short

HARDCODED.rule: found -> the instructor decides (a value with a configuration rationale is allowed)
HARDCODED.why: README: 'Hardcoded buckets, endpoints, account IDs, thresholds, or model IDs without configuration rationale: up to 1 point'

CLAIMS_NOT_DONE.rule: a claimed file that no commit supports -> the instructor decides (never automatic: academic-integrity implications)
CLAIMS_NOT_DONE.why: README: 'Agent reports claim commands or tests that were not actually run: up to 2 points lost and possible academic-integrity review'

TASKFORGE_FORK.rule: control plane mostly copied from the tutorial -> the instructor decides
TASKFORGE_FORK.why: README: 'Only a generic agent tutorial fork with TaskForge renamed ...: zero'

decisions.absent_category: A category that is completely absent (no Spark at all; Hadoop replaced by a local loop) earns none of its points AND takes its README deduction: the deduction is for missing a required component, on top of not earning its points.
decisions.secrets: A possible secret is never deducted automatically: the instructor confirms the value is real first.
decisions.tests: Fewer than 25 meaningful tests: the deduction grows with how far short you are, 2 x (25 - counted) / 25.
decisions.flags: If the automatic verifier flags a verdict (for example: the cited code is not called by the job, or it contradicts a deterministic check), the verdict still counts and the instructor takes a look. Only a verdict the judge could not decide (cannot_tell) is left to the instructor entirely.
